label: Modal Sheet
title: Modal Sheet
summary: Use a Modal Sheet for a task that slides up over the page, such as asking HelloJio, and goes away when it’s done.
corePrinciple: A page over the page, with a clear way to close it.

anatomy.title: A white sheet with one slot
anatomy.description: The sheet is a rounded white surface with one slot. It has no title or close button of its own: put an App Bar with a close button at the top and the main field at the bottom.
blocks: White, with 20 px corners and no handle.
One column of your content; it gets the sheet’s modes, without Page type.
Yours: the top of the slot, holding the close button.
Yours: a named IconButton that hides the sheet.
Yours: the main input or action, at the bottom.
specimen: Ask about your spends, bills, or investments.

configuration.title: Height, scrim, top inset, and page type
configuration.description: A sheet fills the screen by default; fit it to short content instead. A scrim dims the page around a fitted sheet, and a top inset lets the page peek above it. Page type sets the sheet’s colour.
blocks: The default: the sheet covers the screen and the field sits at its foot.
The sheet hugs its content and docks to the bottom.
The page stays bright behind the sheet, as in the Storybook story.
The page peeks 40 px above, and the sheet shortens to keep its bottom on the screen.
MainPage, the default used everywhere else here, and SubPage both give a white sheet.
A light grey sheet. Its text stays dark, and the HelloJio field turns white to stand out.

states.title: Shown, hidden, and how it closes
states.description: The screen shows and hides the sheet: it slides up from the bottom and settles without a bounce, then slides back down. A drag down asks to close it, unless drag to close is turned off. A hidden sheet waits below the screen, out of the Tab order and hidden from screen readers.
blocks: Over a dimmed page, docked to the bottom.
Below the screen; only the page shows.
A drag down does nothing; the X and the scrim still close it, so a stray drag can’t lose a half-typed question.

sizing.title: Full width, filling or fitting the screen
sizing.description: The sheet spans its screen with 12 px of padding at the top, 8 px at the sides, and 32 px at the bottom, and puts 12 px between the items in its slot. It fills the screen’s height unless it fits its content.

sources.title: Use the public Modal Sheet contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (27 October build) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Modal Sheet is one 360 × 728 white surface with one slot. In the package it renders in place until it’s given visible; then it slides over its screen with an optional scrim and can be dragged down. It puts its 12 px gap between the slot’s items, and a top inset shortens the sheet so its bottom stays on the screen. On the web it’s a dialog named by its App Bar title, and a hidden sheet leaves the Tab order. When the screen shows it, focus moves to its first control (the X here) and Tab stays inside; Escape, even from the text field, the X, or the scrim closes it and returns focus to what opened it. trapFocus= turns that off for a sheet shown inside a page, as these examples are until you open them again; In context keeps it. Page type JioPlus turns it light grey and stays off its slot, except the App Bar: text stays dark, and the HelloJio Input turns white to show on the grey. Turning the drag off leaves the X and the scrim. The examples host the sheet as the Storybook story does: on a black screen whose page steps back with the sheet, through the package’s page-stack hook (the screen’s job, not the sheet’s). The screen’s corners are rounder than the sheet’s, like a phone’s. The published Docs page is still the old generated one. The slide runs the package’s own spring settings, as in Storybook.
